intent: B19 of the final-release programme: the release. Full gate, Playwright, mutation survivors reconciled, a browser walk of every screen at 1280x720 and 390x844 on the isolated instance, docs built; package.json to 1.0.0-rc.1 and the tag v1.0.0-rc.1 on dev. The real-Hermes round natively on this machine (decisions 10 and 18): the operator configures the API-key provider in Hermes and on the Models page, hermes gateway run, HERMES_GATEWAY_URL pointed at it, the quest ledger chapters 1 to 7 driven end to end, then the round-6 confirm list, then the Docker profiles. Every finding a defect with the same verify-then-fix loop; rc.2 if any blocker. Then v1.0.0, dev merged to main by the operator's gated release PR (ADR-0006), docs-pages.yml publishing, the operator enabling Pages, README hero and docs/images recaptured.

reasons.evidence: the real-Hermes round calls a paid provider through the operator's own key; tags and the release PR are pushed
the Pages deployment is state outside the repository

programme: B19, depends on B18 (T-0112). Publishing to a new external destination (Pages) and the merge to main are the operator's, per the constitution's approver rule; the session prepares and the operator clicks.
found_by_the_walk: One defect, fixed in this batch, and it was invisible to everything else. At 390x844 the h1 on five screens had a bounding box of 0 x 28: in the DOM, display flex, visibility visible, and nought pixels wide, so a reader on a phone could not tell which page they were on. A jsdom render has no layout, so all 5772 unit tests passed over it, and the 1280-wide walk saw nothing. The cause was three shrink-0 siblings competing with a title group that was allowed to collapse: the actions on Logs measure 388px inside a 390px bar, and on the Rec Room pages the back label took the row one level further in. Fixed by wrapping the bar, letting the title group grow rather than merely shrink, and standing the back label down below sm while it keeps its arrow and gains an unconditional accessible name. tests/e2e/b19-a-title-survives-a-phone.spec.ts pins it at 390 wide, measured red at 5 failed / 2 passed before the fix, and asserts the RENDERED BOX rather than the element existing, because 'the heading is in the document' was true throughout.
remaining: The version bump and the tag v1.0.0-rc.1. Not done: a tag is not a thing to place on the operator's behalf.
v1.0.0, the merge of dev into main, and the Pages deployment. The operator's, per this record's tier and the approver rule.
59 minor and 18 polish findings from the round, recorded in org/reviews/ and in the round's own data. None blocks a release.
found_by_the_docker_profiles: One defect, in the harness rather than the product, and it had been latent since the security batch. `update_preserves_user_data` compares a sha256 listing of the data directory before and after an update and refuses any difference as 'possible data loss'. It failed -- and nothing had been lost: the listing had GAINED ./auth-token. Since authentication began failing closed the app mints that token on first boot, and under --skip-http no server runs during setup, so it is first written during the update. The profiles are only run at release time, which is why nine batches passed over it. Excluding the file would have been the lazy repair, so it leaves the listing the way the other generated files already have and gains an assertion for the two things that would genuinely matter about it: a token that VANISHED locks the operator out of their own install, and one that was ROTATED silently kills the ?ps_token link the installer printed at them. All five branches of that assertion were driven against a stubbed container before it was called done. The failure also could not say which file had moved, which is the one fact needed to judge whether anything was lost; it now names what was removed, added or changed, with removal first.
harness_amendments: Two, both in tests/integration/test_full_install_update_process.py: the manifest stops carrying the generated auth-token and the scenario asserts its existence and its stability instead, and the manifest-mismatch failure now prints the difference rather than only announcing that there was one.
observations_not_acted_on: The dashboard renders its own copy of the header bar rather than using PageHeader, so the narrow-viewport fix in this batch does not reach it. It passes the phone spec today because its title column is a plain div, which will not collapse below its content, and the walk found no overflow there -- so there is no failing case to fix. It remains the same visual element implemented twice, which is the deferred item about the dashboard adopting PageHeader.
real_hermes_round: DONE, on the operator's own machine against a real Hermes agent running MiniMax M3. The agent's API server is a gateway PLATFORM rather than a separate command: API_SERVER_ENABLED plus API_SERVER_KEY in the agent's environment, then `hermes gateway run`, serving /v1 on 8642. PatterStage ran against an isolated data dir and a COPY of the agent home, so nothing in the round could damage the operator's own install. A mission dispatched from the browser reached the agent and returned the right answer in about nine seconds; chat answered in three. THIRTY OF THIRTY-TWO QUESTS were completed against that agent -- every quest this host can run. The two outstanding are the two genuinely blocked here: 3.7 needs a memory provider (the operator's Hermes points at a Hindsight that is not up) and 4.3 needs a host scheduler, which native Windows does not have. Chapters 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7 are complete.
round_findings: Seven testers drove the seven chapters in parallel: 105 findings confirmed by a second reader, 5 refuted, and 61 things recorded as working, because a release needs to know its own value and those are what a change must not break. One blocker, 27 majors. Written up for a person to read at org/reviews/2026-09-real-hermes-round.md. THE BLOCKER: the starter workflow the quest ledger points a newcomer at reported success without writing its summary. A terminal stage is where a run STOPS -- applyNext completes on reaching one without dispatching it -- and the seed had marked the documentation stage that does the work as terminal. Three things made it durable: the author already knew (the next workflow down carries a comment about the same trap and is built correctly), the suite ASSERTED the defect and so locked it in, and the guide told the user the opposite. Fixed in the seed, in the Build tab so no operator can rebuild it by hand, and in the seeder so installs that already booted repair themselves -- a keyed seed writes nothing on an install that already has the workflow, so without that last part it would have been permanent for every existing user. Proved on a live run: three node runs, `write` in the context, a real summary produced.
what_the_fixes_covered: Money: `every 0m` was accepted and built an unbounded loop of paid runs; Story Weaver's Stop did not stop a retry, left the reader stale so the next write billed the wrong chapter, and recorded a stop as a provider timeout with config-debugging advice; and the Rec Room never said what a story cost. Honesty: the spend tooltip claimed published per-model rates when the rate table is a short static list and every figure on this install came from the fallback. Chat's 'model not ready' banner fired on a working install off a registry default chat does not use; three screens gave three different answers to 'do I have a model'; the Active badge named a model the agent was not running; a skills count was wrong by two orders of magnitude. Memory errors said 'HTTP 500', which became 'fetch failed', which the repo itself calls "Node's phrasing, not an instruction to anybody". Navigation: ten strings in src/ and seven in docs/ sent readers to sections the regroup retired. And one control that did not exist: three places told the operator to choose a memory provider on the Memory page, and there was no chooser anywhere in the product. The capability was never missing, only the control.
the_review_pass_earned_its_place: Twice, and it is worth recording because the lesson is about fixing rather than finding. One fix deleted the false 'published per-model rates' claim from the spend console and left a comment asking for it not to be restored; a concurrent fix put that exact sentence into a NEW component, over the one figure that can never come from a rate on file, because a story run records no model at all. A rule held in one component is not held: there is now a test that forbids the claim anywhere in the source, measured red against the real violation. A second fix, whose brief was honest and actionable copy, shipped a sentence telling the user to choose a different provider on a screen that had no such control, and coupled an unreadable config.yaml to a 500 that took down the entire Models page. Both were caught by the reviewer with a probe rather than an argument, and both are fixed.
verification: The pre-tag verification the plan asks for is complete and green on dev at 119cce29. Gate by exit code: lint 0, tsc 0, jest 0 (5772 tests, 575 suites), knip 0, canary 0, build 0, Playwright 140 passed and 25 skipped. Docs built: 77 pages, and the site opens from file:// with its rail, its prose and its images. The release walk covered every one of the 25 rail screens at BOTH 1280x720 and 390x844 -- 50 screen-loads -- asking of each whether it renders its own heading, says anything at all, carries a title and a working ?, scrolls sideways, or logs a console error, plus whether the rail fits at 720 tall. It now reports no findings. The Docker harnesses are green too: the deploy-API restart smoke passes, and the install and update harness passes BOTH profiles -- smoke 5/5 and release 11/11, the latter covering restart, rebuild, both install paths and the two update-data scenarios. After the round: lint 0, tsc 0, jest 0 (6090 tests, 615 suites), knip 0, build 0, Playwright 140 passed. A live verification against the real agent on the fixed build: the money-burning schedule refused with a message true of both schedule kinds, the Models page surviving a config problem, the Memory page carrying the provider chooser the rest of the product points at, no retired section name on any screen checked, and no screen claiming a published rate. The one 503 in that run is the memory route correctly refusing with the sentence this round gave it, on a machine where no memory provider is running. The Docker install and update harness is complete on every profile it has: smoke 5/5, release 11/11, and release with the real upstream installer 12/12, the last of which pulls the NousResearch install over the network and was the final verification item that was not the operator's.
